description: Three demo goals for the Bookshelf API, pre-decomposed into intents with scripted reference solutions (agents/solutions/<intent>.mjs). Interactions are designed and verified by scripts/verify-scenarios.mjs.

goals.text: Make every Bookshelf request observable: traceable ids, version info on /health, catalog metrics, and stable error codes.

intents.title: Tag every request with an x-request-id and log it
intents.reasoning: Support cannot join a customer's report to our logs. Reuse the caller's x-request-id (or cf-ray) when present so traces join across hops; otherwise mint a UUID. Echo it on the response and add it to the access-log line.

intents.title: Report build version and uptime on /health
intents.reasoning: After a deploy we cannot tell which build is serving. Expose a semver VERSION and uptimeSeconds; keep ok:true so existing probes stay green.

intents.title: Expose catalog gauges at GET /metrics
intents.reasoning: Dashboards need book/author counts without querying the API page by page. Prometheus text format is what our scraper speaks. Registered in the route table only; no middleware change.

intents.title: Add stable machine-readable codes to error bodies
intents.reasoning: Clients string-match error messages, so every wording change breaks them. Add an additive `code` field derived from the status; keep `error` as the human message.

goals.text: Make the catalog nicer to browse: author bibliographies, fewer round trips per page, forgiving search, and valid ISBNs.

intents.title: List an author's books at GET /authors/:id/books
intents.reasoning: The author page currently fetches all books and filters client-side. Serve it directly, paged, with its own page default so it does not couple to /books paging.

intents.title: Raise the /books default page size from 20 to 30
intents.reasoning: The mobile list shows ~28 rows per screen, so a 20-item page forces a second request on first paint. 30 fills the screen in one round trip.

intents.title: Make ?q= case-insensitive substring search
intents.reasoning: Users type 'dune' and get nothing because search is a case-sensitive prefix match. Match anywhere in the title, ignoring case.

intents.title: Reject ISBN-13s with a bad checksum
intents.reasoning: Typos in ISBNs break the cover-image lookup downstream. Validate the ISBN-13 checksum at write time; hyphens and spaces are allowed.

goals.text: Harden the API for public launch: rotatable API keys, bounded pages, rate limiting, request latency in logs, and a CORS allowlist.

intents.title: Accept a list of API keys so keys rotate without downtime
intents.reasoning: Rotating the single API_KEY breaks every client at once. Accept a comma-separated list (new key first, old key until clients move); compare against every key so timing does not reveal the slot.

intents.title: Cap list pages at 25 items
intents.reasoning: A 50-item page is the largest single response we serve and will be the largest D1 read after the migration. Bound payload size at 25.

intents.title: Rate-limit clients per IP (429 past the limit)
intents.reasoning: One scraper can starve the isolate. A fixed-window per-IP limit (RATE_LIMIT/min, default 600) sheds abuse; it sits inside CORS so browsers can read the 429. Wired into the middleware chain only; no route change.

intents.title: Log request latency (durationMs) on every access-log line
intents.reasoning: We cannot see slow endpoints before launch. Measure around next() with performance.now() and add durationMs to the access-log line.

intents.title: Restrict CORS to an origin allowlist when configured
intents.reasoning: `*` lets any site call write endpoints from a logged-in browser. When CORS_ORIGINS is set, echo only listed origins (with Vary: Origin); unset keeps `*` so local dev is unchanged.

interactions.narrative: Both declare src/index.ts, so declare_intent returns each as the other's overlap before any code is written. They edit different regions (g1-metrics: an import after the health import + a route-table line; g3-rate-limit: an import after the logging import + the middleware-chain line), so git merges cleanly and the combined suite is green. Demo beat: Q1 awareness ('agent 2 is changing src/index.ts because ...').

Both rewrite formatLogLine's signature, its JSON.stringify line, and the body of withLogging. Whichever lands second hits a real git conflict in src/middleware/logging.ts. Resolution is replay: re-derive g3-log-latency on the new trunk with g1-request-id's reasoning in context (agents/apply.mjs g3-log-latency --replay-on g1-request-id), which logs both requestId and durationMs and passes CI. Demo beat: Q2 conflicts.

Disjoint footprints (no declare-time overlap), clean git merge, each green alone. Together DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE 30 > MAX_PAGE_SIZE 25: parseLimit clamps the default to 25, so the page-size contract test and g2's own accept check fail on the combined SHA. Only train CI on the exact combined SHA catches it; bisect isolates the pair. Demo beat: Q2 'one lane fails CI on the combined SHA, so it bisects'.

failingTests: contract: the default page size is servable
GET /books without ?limit= returns exactly DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE items
GET /books returns 30 books per page by default

interactions.narrative: The only intent whose footprint matches a protected glob (src/auth/** in .flare/policy.yml). It stops at awaiting_plan until a human approves the plan (one click). Demo beat: 'Goal -> plan'.

trains.narrative: Everything except the second half of each conflicting pair: 11 of 13 intents, 2 of them overlapping on src/index.ts. Merges cleanly and is green.
Everything except g3-log-latency (the textual conflict): 12 of 13 intents merge cleanly but CI is red; bisect isolates g2-default-page-size + g3-max-page-size.
